messages:
mina: Heads-up — we're bringing up a new candidate (caldera-8b from HoriNet). License language looks odd: 'Non-commercial use only; hosting allowed for research & inference endpoints with attribution'. Can we serve a quantized derivative to paying customers via Hosted API? cc @sophie

sophie: Short answer: probably not without an explicit commercial license. That phrase is ambiguous — 'hosting allowed for research' likely means non-commercial hosting. Need the full text. Please paste the exact clauses.

mina: Pasting the relevant snippet we were given:
```
License X v1.2
Section 3.1: Non-commercial use only.
Section 5: Derivative works and hosting: "Redistribution and hosting of modified weights permitted for non-commercial research and inference endpoints with attribution to original authors."
```
So two questions: 1) does serving quantized weights via our Hosted API count as "hosting"/"redistribution"? 2) does paid access (= commercial) violate 3.1 even if Section 5 mentions hosting for inference endpoints?

legal-bot: Auto-scan summary: risk_level=high; license contains a non-commercial clause (3.1) that supersedes permissive derivatives. Section 5's "hosting permitted for non-commercial..." creates an exception only for non-commercial inference. Recommendation: do NOT enable this model on Hosted (commercial) product. Allow only non-commercial evaluation and private deployments where customer controls weights and commercial obligations are explicit.

chris: From infra's POV: we need to know whether providing quantized weights in a container or cache is considered "redistribution" under the license. If yes, even Dedicated (we host infra for the customer) could be risky unless the customer supplies the original weights and we never store/ship modified files. Suggest we treat "shipping quantized weights" as redistribution until legal says otherwise.

mina: Also found this clause about attribution: "Attribution must be included in any UI or API response metadata when serving derivative models." Do we have a plan to surface that attribution automatically?

chris: We can add attribution metadata in the response headers and Console model info page. But legal needs to confirm the exact wording for what counts as "attribution" (in-line mention vs footer).

sophie: Legal guidance: 1) this license is non-commercial — commercial hosting is not permitted. 2) Section 5 only grants hosting for non-commercial inference, so paid Hosted API usage violates 3.1. 3) Redistribution (including shipping quantized weights) appears restricted. Our safe path: a) block model in Hosted product, b) allow Private if customer supplies weights and signs indemnity/commercial addendum, c) Dedicated may be allowed only if we do not distribute modified weight files and we have vendor commercial license.

eng-ml-oncall: Practical ops notes: our quantization experiments so far (INT8) show ~4% ROUGE drop on summarization vs fp16. If we cannot host commercially, we should still run quant evals behind a feature-flag for internal benchmarking and vendor negotiations. Also: add a webhook to upstream repo so license changes trigger automatic re-eval of gating.

chris: Proposed model-registry checklist (short):
- source_license_url: <link>
- commercial_ok: yes/no
- redistribution_ok: yes/no
- attribution_required: free-text
- allowed_deployments: [hosted, dedicated, private]
- required_license_addendum: <link or NONE>
I'll open a PR to add these fields and enforce Hosted gating if commercial_ok != yes.

mina: Action items summary: @sophie confirm final ruling and draft addendum language; @chris add registry flags + block Hosted by default; @mina reach out to HoriNet about commercial license and run quant/quality evals under feature-flag. I'll add a ticket for attribution UI work. Thanks all :thumbsup:

legal-bot: Noted. Creating ticket LEG-2026 to track vendor outreach and license clearance.

mina: Closing loop — will update this thread after vendor reply.
